items.question: A 16 by 16 map, a 3 by 3 kernel, padding 1, stride 2. What is the output side?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Use the output-size formula.

byKey.same: Padding 1 keeps the size only at stride 1.

items.question: A 5 by 5 convolution from 4 channels to 6 filters. How many parameters?

byKey.no-cin: Each filter has a 5 by 5 kernel per input channel.

explain.text: $4 \times 25 = 100$ weights and 1 bias per filter, 6 filters: 606.

items.question: Conv 3 by 3, max pool 2 by 2 (stride 2), conv 3 by 3, max pool 2 by 2, conv 3 by 3; every conv at stride 1. What is the side of the receptive field of the last layer?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Each layer adds $(k - 1)$ times the strides before it.

byKey.no-stride: You added $k - 1$ for each layer but ignored the strides of the pools. After a pool, one step is 2 pixels.
byKey.product: Receptive fields grow by adding, not multiplying.

explain.text: The jump between neighbouring outputs is 1, then 2 after the first pool, then 4. The layers add $2, 1, 4, 2, 8$ to the starting 1: 18.

items.prose: A 2 by 2 max-pool window holds $\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 7 \\ 5 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and receives a gradient of 3.
items.question: What gradient does the 5 receive?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Which entry set the pooled value?

byKey.avg: That spreads the gradient as average pooling does.
byKey.all: Only the winner gets the gradient.

explain.text: The pooled value is 7; nudging the 5 changes nothing, so its gradient is 0 and the 7 gets all 3.

items.question: A 2 by 2 average pool receives a gradient of 0.8 at one output. What gradient reaches each of its four inputs?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Each input has weight $\tfrac14$.

byKey.all: Each input moved the mean by a quarter.

items.question: im2col of a 2-channel 6 by 6 image, 3 by 3 kernels, no padding, stride 1. What shape is the patch matrix?

options.why: Each row holds both channels’ windows: 18 values.

items.question: Which padding keeps the size for a 9 by 9 kernel at stride 1?
A 3 by 3 convolution from 2 channels to 4 filters on an 8 by 8 map with padding 1. How many multiply-adds?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Positions times $k^2 c_{\text{in}}$ times $c_{\text{out}}$.

byKey.one-channel: Each dot product runs over both input channels: 18 terms.

items.question: A 10-wide input, a 3-wide kernel, stride 3, no padding. How many outputs, and how many columns are never read? Choose the pair.

options.why: The windows cover columns 0 to 8; column 9 is left.
A fourth window would start at 9 and need columns 9 to 11.

explain.text: Windows cover 0 to 2, 3 to 5 and 6 to 8; column 9 is dropped.
